title: Standardize engineering artifacts across agents

summary.answer: A compatibility path bypassed Semantic contract.
summary.context: Today skills/agent-artifacts/ and src/agent_artifacts/schemas/ each decide which sections an artifact must carry on their own.
summary.what_changes_it: A second occurrence after the bypass in skills/agent-artifacts/ is deleted.

impact: A required decision, risk, or validation step disappears because the generated layout changes.
detection: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review at 09:12. Connecting that symptom to the bypass in skills/agent-artifacts/ took 25 more minutes.

timeline.event: First invalid result reached the consumer
timeline.signal: Scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review.

root_cause: The compatibility path skipped Semantic contract, so Artifact engine ran without the rejection rules the design assumed.
contributing_factors: The old path stayed reachable after rollout
No fixture asserted a terminal record per caller
resolution: Disabled the compatibility path. Routed the caller through Semantic contract and reconciled CLI and MCP adapters.

actions.verification: No direct Agent skill to Artifact engine call remains
Alert fires when scenario regression lacks a required semantic section or fails visual review

lessons: A healthy boundary is no proof that callers used it
Compatibility paths need an owner and a deletion condition on day one
counterfactuals: A test asserting one terminal event per request would have blocked the release
subtitle: A caller skipped the boundary, so a rendered artifact shipped without its risk section.
invariants: Artifact engine never runs on a context Semantic contract rejected.
Two requests never share one semanticContractRunId.
A failed check never reaches CLI and MCP adapters.
